AnalyticsActivityBucket.description: One time bucket. Besides timestamp, the keys are per event: total_<event> and unique_<event>. An event with no activity in a bucket is omitted rather than returned as zero.

timestamp.description: YYYY-MM-DD for day, 'Week of YYYY-MM-DD' for week, YYYY-MM for month

access_token.description: Bearer token to use in Authorization header

scope.description: Present only for super-user tokens. Value: 'super'. Requests using this token must include X-Account-GUID header.

eligible.description: Subset of total that can actually be emailed

total.description: Contacts in the target lists minus the exclude lists, before any eligibility check

Blast.description: A flat record combining sequence and message data for blast-type sequences.

can_email_code.description: Machine-readable code indicating why can_email was changed (e.g. 'manual', 'bounce', 'unsubscribe')

can_email_message.description: Human-readable message describing why can_email was changed

id.description: Contact GUID — use this as the identifier in all API calls

options.description: Arbitrary key-value attributes stored on the contact. Present only when set.

segment_code.description: Per-contact segment label used by the send engine to pick newsletter variants. Sourced from CRM (Salesforce/HubSpot) per-list mappings.

segment_source.description: Newsletter membership view only. Which precedence layer produced segment_code, highest first: 'assigned' (explicit, sticky), 'newsletter_rule', 'list', 'contact', 'rule'. Null when the contact has no segment. Distinct from the 'source' field above, which is the contact's own origin.

ContactBulkCreateBody.description: Envelope for POST /contacts/bulk. Each element follows the same shape as ContactCreateBody.

contacts.description: Contacts to create. Must contain between 1 and 1000 items.

ContactBulkResultItem.description: Per-item outcome from POST /contacts/bulk. `contact` is populated when status is 'created'; `error` is populated when status is 'failed'.

error.description: Reason this item failed (only present when status='failed')

index.description: Zero-based position of this item in the request's contacts array

can_email.description: Sets the contact's emailability. Applied whether this POST creates a new contact or matches an existing active contact by email. Defaults to true on creation when omitted.

identifier.description: The contact's ID (value) in the external system — the key resolution matches on. Must be provided together with `system`.

list_id.description: Add the contact to this list immediately

options.description: Arbitrary key-value attributes stored on the contact. Persisted only when this POST creates a new contact; ignored when an active contact already exists for the email (same as first_name/last_name/source). Use PUT /contacts/{id} to merge options into an existing contact.

segment_code.description: Per-contact segment label used by the send engine to pick newsletter variants. Sourced from the CRM segment field mapping on the list (Salesforce/HubSpot).

subscriptions.description: Optional subscriptions to create for the contact. Each entry upserts a canonical subscription (no integration) on (contact_id, subscription_type_id): if one already exists its can_email is updated rather than a duplicate being inserted.

system.description: External system name: 'hubspot' (and other 3rd-party CRMs), 'csv', 'newsletter', or 'rex'. Must be provided together with `identifier` to create an external identifier record.

system_identifier.description: Scope the identifier is unique within. REQUIRED when system='newsletter' (the newsletter guid). IGNORED for all other systems: 'hubspot'/3rd-party/'csv' are scoped to the account automatically, and 'rex' has no scope. Do not send a HubSpot portal id, a filename, or the id value itself.

ContactCreateSubscriptionItem.description: A subscription to create alongside a contact via POST /contacts. status_changed, is_active, and integration_id are set server-side.

can_email.description: Whether this subscription is emailable. Accepts 0/1 or true/false.

can_email_code.description: Machine-readable code indicating why can_email was changed

can_email_message.description: Human-readable message describing why can_email was changed

identifier.description: The contact's ID (value) in the external system — the key resolution matches on. Required when `system` is provided.

options.description: Key-value attributes to merge into the contact's existing options. Input values take precedence; keys not in the request are preserved. Set a key to null to delete just that key. An empty object, null, or non-object value is a no-op — the stored options blob is never wholesale cleared.

segment_code.description: Replace the contact's segment label. Send an empty string to clear it; omit the key (a JSON null is treated as omitted) to leave the stored value alone.

system.description: External system name: 'hubspot' (and other 3rd-party CRMs), 'csv', 'newsletter', or 'rex'. When provided with `identifier`, upserts an external identifier linking this contact to the external system.

system_identifier.description: Scope the identifier is unique within. REQUIRED when system='newsletter' (the newsletter guid). IGNORED for all other systems: 'hubspot'/3rd-party/'csv' are scoped to the account automatically, and 'rex' has no scope. Do not send a HubSpot portal id, a filename, or the id value itself.

identifier.description: The contact's ID (value) in the external system

system_identifier.description: The scope the identifier is unique within: the newsletter guid for 'newsletter', 'rasa-account:<account id>' for account-scoped systems, or null for 'rex'

InsightsAction.description: One engagement event. Keys the source stream does not carry are absent rather than null.

confidence.description: 0 when the click looked automated, else 1

newsletters.description: How many of the account's newsletters this contact belongs to

effective_date.description: The week the cloud was built for

entity.description: The run's subject: campaign_integration ID for crm_sync, newsletter GUID for newsletter syncs

run_attributes.description: Run results: counts, error summary, artifact paths (JSON)

system.description: External system the run synced against, e.g. 'HubSpot'; null when not applicable

options.description: Arbitrary key-value attributes stored on the list (e.g. `{"source_type": "ftp"}`).

RemovedContact.description: A tombstone row: enough identity to match the legacy record, plus when/why the contact was removed.

archived_date.description: When the contact was removed. PROXY: Contact.updated / ContactList.updated until a dedicated archived_at column exists.

email.description: Contact email — always present; the primary key for matching the legacy record

is_archived.description: True = the contact is archived globally (gone from every list — purge it); False = the contact is still live but was dropped from the list(s) in scope (unlink just that membership)

newsletter_id.description: Per-newsletter legacy identifier (external_identifier where system='newsletter'), when known

record_count.description: Number of records in THIS page of results. Not a grand total — use total_query_count for that.

total_count.description: Total records associated with the resource, ignoring filters. On the messaging /contacts sub-endpoints this is every contact in the target lists regardless of status.

total_query_count.description: Total records matching the request's filters, across all pages. Null unless the endpoint supplies it: the messaging /contacts sub-endpoints always do, /contacts requires include_counts=1.

Segment.description: An account-level segment — an entry in the account's catalog of valid segment codes.

rule_attribute.description: Contact-attribute key for the optional account-level match rule

SegmentAssignBody.description: Body for assigning/clearing a contact's segment in a newsletter.

segment_code.description: A defined account segment code to assign (sticky). A blank/empty value clears the assignment so the contact falls through to lower-precedence rules.

cleared.description: True when the assignment was removed

identity_replicated.description: Whether the identity-side replica was updated (best-effort)

segment_code.description: The assigned code, or null when cleared

pause.description: Whether to pause the sequence at this message

time_since.description: Days since previous message before this one can be sent

Subscription.description: Subscription summary embedded in a Contact (GET /contacts/{id})

contact_id.description: Contact GUID or integer contact ID (both are returned by GET /contacts)

synced_at.description: Timestamp of last sync from external system. Defaults to now.

SubscriptionFull.description: Full subscription record returned by the /subscriptions endpoints

account_guid.description: Super-user clients only: campaign account GUID to scope this token to. Omit to receive an unscoped super-user token that requires X-Account-GUID on every request.

post.description:
Creates up to 1000 contacts in a single request. Each item is processed independently within its own database SAVEPOINT, so a failure on one row (e.g. missing email) does not stop the rest of the batch. The response returns a per-item status with either the created contact or an error message.

Returns 201 if at least one item was created. Returns 400 if the envelope is invalid (missing `contacts` array, empty array, more than 1000 items) or if every item failed.

201.description: Bulk processed. Inspect per-item status in results.

400.description: Invalid envelope, empty array, more than 1000 items, or all items failed

get.description: Tombstone counterpart to GET /contacts?list_id=<id>. Returns contacts that have left the list — either dropped from it (ContactList.is_archived) or archived globally (Contact.is_archived) — so a sync consumer can reconcile removals incrementally via archived_since instead of diffing a full snapshot. is_archived distinguishes the two modes (gone globally vs only off this list). NOTE: archived_date is a proxy (Contact.updated / ContactList.updated — the row's last-modified time, which for an archival is the archival time) until a dedicated archived_at column exists, mirroring the v1 /persons/deleted feed.

parameters.name: list_id

parameters.name: archived_since

400.description: Missing/invalid list_id, or invalid archived_since

delete.description: Permanently deletes the contact, along with the personal data held for them: their name, email address, list memberships, subscriptions and any external identifiers. This is an undoable action and should be reserved for uses such as GDPR erasure. It is not the action to use for unsubscribing a contact, or for taking one off a list - to remove a contact from a single list without deleting them, use DELETE /contact-lists/{id}/list/{list_id}. The deletion covers every newsletter of this account the contact belongs to, not only the one it was added through; memberships of the same person in other accounts' newsletters are left alone. Pass full_delete=true (super tokens only) for a person-driven erasure that removes every membership the person holds across all accounts, together with every contact holding their email addresses in any account. Deletion is not atomic: the response reports the outcome of each stage, and a stage that cannot complete is reported there rather than undoing the stages that already succeeded. A contact that cannot be fully deleted is archived instead, and the response says why; once the cause is fixed the same request can be repeated, since this endpoint also accepts contacts that are already archived.

parameters.description: When true, erase this person everywhere: every newsletter membership they hold across all accounts, and every contact holding their email addresses in any account. Requires a super token; other tokens receive 403.
parameters.name: full_delete

post.description:
OAuth2 Client Credentials grant. Returns a Bearer access token.

**Regular clients:** token is scoped to the client's account — no additional parameters needed.

**Super-user clients** (account_id 10000): two options:
- Pass `account_guid` in the request body to receive a token scoped to that specific campaign account.
- Omit `account_guid` to receive an unscoped super-user token (`scope: super`). All subsequent requests using this token must include an `X-Account-GUID` header with the target campaign account GUID.

400.description: Bad request — missing or invalid fields
